entry.text: No, no, not smoking again. Just... need the smell. Aromatherapy, let's call it. Works wonders for stress.
And today's going to be a stressful one, I'm afraid.

click.text: Sorry, {{name_yves}}, not much time for chatting today.

response.text: Ah. Well. Bad news - some ominous auditor-type priest from the city is heading this way.
Worse news - he's not supposed to know the organ ever stopped working, because Jean-Noël, apparently, got creative again.
Good news - yesterday we actually finished mending what needed mending. Everything's fixed. Individually. Collectively... not so much.
...And that makes it bad news again. Some of those bits we worked on in the workshop still need to be hauled back, installed, tuned and blessed. Even if we run, it'll take all day.
So now the Sisters and Father are busy thinking up ways to stall the watchdog, while Pierrick and I try to wrap it up before he pokes his holy nose inside.
To be honest... Maybe it'd be cleaner if they did find out. It's been a long run of small lies and quiet cover-ups.
You said you quit. I'm just protecting your precious diaphragm.
Oh? Actively undermining your own profit margin. That's new.
...But fine. I'll take my stress without accompaniment this time.

next.text: But... I don't want to be the one who'll start that fire.

next_bellowsAsked.text: But... I played my part in this mess too. So I'm probably not the one to decide who deserves to burn.
Or maybe I'm just a coward.

toooth.text: Oh, that's an interesting thing. You want me to take that tooth?

response.text: Alright then. If that's what you want.
Fair enough. Doesn't sound like the kind of matter I'm meant to carry around anyway.

wrong_items.text: Creative interpretation, {{name_yves}}, but I asked for something else.

wrong_price.text: Off by a few notes. You might want to tune that till.

wrong_price_yvesAbigail.text: So my wife was right about you people with funny letters?

checkout.text: Ahh, what a fine day we've got lined up.
If we make it through alive, my wife roped me and Félix into that concert at Expresso. Not exactly wild youth entertainment, sitting with us old folks, but if you get bored, come by.

zub_pierrick5ToothTaken.text: Ah, really? That's... good. Yeah. It's better that way.
Thanks. That means a lot for me.

zub_yvesToothTaken.text: ...I gave the jar to Yves, the organ repairman.
Oh. The repairman? The older one?
Mm. Not his. But maybe he'll... figure it out. Yeah. Anyway, thanks for trying.

zub.text: ...No luck finding who the tooth belonged to.
Oh. Okay. That's... okay. I tried. I mean, you tried. Thanks for that.

order.text: Let me buy you a pack of whatever you smoke. As a thanks. Put them with mine.

options.text: I think I've earned the tooth backstory

response.text: Uhh... I just imagined if someone stole my tooth and- I don't know, it felt creepy. You don't just keep a stranger's tooth, right?
I don't even know why I got so attached to it. I just... did. And that sort of thing never ends well.

options.text: You can have it back, if you want

response.text: Oh. Okay. Great. Huh. You still have it?
No, but you can come pick it up. Tonight at Expresso.
What? No. Why the hell would he-
No. No-no...
...I mean, I do want it back, but I can't just-
Aargh. That's a terrible idea.
I'll... think about it.
Menthol Morleys. Thought you'd remember by now.
Menthol Morleys. Thought you'd remember by now.
Girl... How would I know.

story.text: Well. That night was a mess. My first week here, I hadn't slept in two days, and they were already short on hands, so I got sent out with the ambulance crew.
We got a call from an old landlady. She said she'd heard this awful crash upstairs, went to shout at the tenant, and found him on the floor with a rope round his neck. Said he looked gone already.

When we got there, the man was barely conscious, looked properly tragic and pale enough to pass for dead, but breathing fine and far too warm for a corpse. Seems the chandelier gave out before he did.
We packed him in anyway, just so he wouldn't, you know, have another go.

On the way out... I noticed something small and white on the floor. His tooth. Just sitting there in the dust, stupid and innocent, like it didn't understand what any of it meant. Probably fell out when he hit his face on the way down, or... I-I don't know. Doesn't matter.
So I took it. Didn't even think much, just slipped it into my pocket like some idiot magpie, and got back in the car.

wrong_items.text: Menthol Morleys. Thought I'd remember by now.

checkout_yestooth.text: One pack for me, one for you. Thank you again, {{name_mado}}.

entry.text: ...Ash returns to the tray, and somehow so do we.

response.text: Mhm. I try to vary the repertoire.
Besides, the day seems intent on staging its own spectacle.
Mhm. Today I intend to be a model of quiet virtue and administrative beauty.

options.text: Sorry if I hit a nerve last time

response.text: You did. Briefly.
But I recovered with admirable grace.
Let us file it under... routine parish disturbance, and quietly close the folder.
Ah, yes, our audience expands. A gentleman with an unshakeable belief in justice and a gift for tidy endings has been sent our way.
Give him a week and he'll return everything to its "proper" shape.
Now... we find out whether what we've been holding together was meant to hold.
If our guest wanders long enough, he will find music. If he walks too quickly, he will find truth.
...And we will be whatever remains after that.

options.text: How did it end up like this?

response.text: Yellow Fleuries, please.

endup.text: Nothing spectacular... Just people and small choices.

endup_someoneSolved.text: How does anything end up anywhere? Love is misplaced. Hurt is misplaced. Someone old grows tired and someone young grows restless.
And someone... keeps the film running. Adjusts the focus a little. Calls the flicker intentional.
Even when the ending is inevitable...
The organ had a beautiful death, I think. It was uneven and stubborn, and it wasn't alone.
*chuckle* Naturally, an ending that neat isn't quite our style. We don't let things leave so easily.

toooth.text: Take it back. I've already got too many pieces of others.

wrong_items.text: Not quite the sacrament I requested.

checkout.text: Now then... I believe I'll go and be difficult to locate for a while. I hear they're projecting something in three dimensions at the cinema.

entry.text: Ah! A tobacconist. Excellent. I was hoping the trail would lead somewhere honest.
A place where everyone passes through, but no one stays... Perfect for observing patterns without interference.
You see, I'm attempting to locate Father Jean-Noël, yet every individual I ask points me somewhere new.
So either he's extraordinarily mobile... or I'm observing coordinated misdirection.
Father Léo, Diocese of Villebourg. I specialise in resolving structural irregularities.

response.text: Strong name. Biblical, but not in an apocalyptic way.
Strong opening move.
Fish? Oh, I love fish!

leoCigs_shooshoo.text: In fact, I may already know something about you. One witness spoke of "a tobacconist standing between the town's youth and tobacco."

leoCardShoo_lavenderless.text: ...Though I confess I'd constructed a rather more formidable mental image.

leoCardShoo.text: Father Léo paused, his eyes lingering on the counter for a moment.
...It's always comforting when people are exactly as decent as you'd hoped.

leoCigs.text: In fact, I may already have your preliminary profile. I did hear reports of a tobacconist willing to overlook certain age restrictions.

leoCardSold.text: Father Léo paused, his eyes lingering on the counter for a moment.
....Hm. But I do enjoy it when first impressions refuse to become conclusions.

next_lavenderless.text: Ah, but I do hope I haven't made you uncomfortable. Priests are supposed to lighten the burdens souls carry around, not hand them another one...
I do believe people have a charming habit of deviating from their expected behaviour mid-investigation.
Still! Patterns are what get you to that moment in the first place, so I try not to abandon them prematurely.

next.text: Moments like that are what keep me taking blasphemy cases. They always open with something enormous...
...and then, more often than not, the entire affair resolves itself into a quiet, slightly embarrassed shared prayer.
...Or a reconciliation arm wrestling match! I employed that method in one particularly stubborn parish dispute over unauthorised hymn additions... Though that's an entirely different story.
Now then, back to this one. I've been promised... eucharistic concerns, auditory concerns, and a seal. That's rather nice.
If you were me, what would you do first?

response.text: Ah. I see. An invitation to abandon the trail.
Now I'm absolutely certain I'm on the right one...
But yes, you're quite right. I shouldn't keep him waiting.
Naturally. The scene itself.
And that's why, before touching anything else, I need the priest this all seems to pass through.
Ah, yes, I would very much like to meet the seal. I imagine it's quite pleasant.
But there's someone far more important I need to see first.
Ah, but I wanted to get to know everyone first.
Mass only lasts an hour... The parish happens the rest of the week.
Besides, there's someone here I'd quite like to meet properly before anything else.
...Ah, right. No, I apologise.
I've already committed to something else.

end.text: Well then. Where would you send me to find Father Jean-Noël, please?

options.text: I'd try that eel thing at the docks

response.text: Y-yeah, docks, definitely. They put up something about some kind of gathering tonight.
Communal gathering... High attendance probability.
Right, yeah. Pretty high. Elle's giving out eel soup, so half the town, probably. At least. And your, um... target... he'd probably end up there with everyone else.
Hm. Promising.
They've already started, though. And once the food's gone, people just drift off, so... if you were going to try, now's probably the time...
...I see.
Your voice changed. Like you're improvising, or... omitting something.
But I did catch someone mentioning eel on the way here, so I guess you're not inventing it entirely. And gatherings like that do tend to be useful. I can work with that.
...That is an implausible lead.
Implausible... but not impossible.
And the combination of its improbability and the certainty in your tone makes me want to risk trusting it.
I see. That's alright.
In that case, I'll keep searching and see what the next lead reveals.

end.text: That gives me enough to proceed. Thank you, {{name_leo}}.
Do enjoy the rest of your day... and {{leo6cigs}}.

I'm leaving.

Beautiful. Really brings the parish together.

organ_organComplete.text: That was me. I punched it.

response.text: Yeah, yeah. Never stopped believing in me, did you?

organ_someoneSolved.text: Then it turned out you weren't the only person around here capable of fucking up a church organ.

Heh. Still, nice to know the parish found someone else to blame for a change.

organ.text: Honestly, I didn't dig into any of that shit.

keyboard.text: Why the fuck did you punch an organ?
Eh. I'd had a shit evening. Spent half of it digging a grave, wanted to go home, you know how it is.
Then I passed the statue of Mary and noticed some moron had stuck this horrible sticky shit all over her hands.
Remembered I'd hidden an emergency knife inside the organ ages ago and figured I'd scrape it off. Looked inside, knife's fucking gone.
So you punished the organ for losing your knife?
I said I'd had a shit evening.
The worst part was it didn't even give me a proper angry organ noise or anything. Just clacked at me.
Think you're supposed to pull those knob things out first if you want it to make noise, genius.
Those knob things. Wow. Organ expert now?
Shut up. I read a newspaper.
Anyway, the clack pissed me off more, so I grabbed something heavy that was lying around and hit it again. That one made a noise.
So yeah. That's what happened to your keyboard.

next.text: Whatever. I should get back to the church and check on Jean-Noël before you waste any more of my evening.
